citeAs: Lin, T.-Y., Maire, M., Belongie, S., Bourdev, L., Girshick, R., Hays, J., Perona, P., Ramanan, D., Zitnick, C. L., & Dollár, P. (2014). Microsoft COCO: Common Objects in Context. ECCV.
creator: Tsung-Yi Lin, Michael Maire, Serge Belongie, Lubomir Bourdev, Ross Girshick, James Hays, Pietro Perona, Deva Ramanan, C. Lawrence Zitnick, Piotr Dollár
description: A large-scale dataset for object recognition and scene understanding, containing images of complex everyday scenes with common objects in their natural context. It includes 2.5 million labeled instances across 91 object categories in 328k images, with per-instance segmentations.
name: Microsoft COCO: Common Objects in Context
rai:annotationsPerItem: Category labeling: 8 workers per image. Instance spotting: 8 workers per image. Instance segmentation: 1 worker per instance. Captions: 5 per image.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Worker precision and recall were compared to expert workers (co-authors). Ground truth was computed using majority vote of experts. For segmentation verification, each segmentation was shown to 3-5 annotators, and discarded if it did not receive at least 4 out of 5 favorable votes.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The pipeline has 3 tasks: (a) category labeling using a hierarchical approach, (b) instance spotting by placing a cross on each instance, and (c) instance segmentation using a modified OpenSurfaces interface. Workers had to complete a training task for each object category before segmenting.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset explicitly mitigates the bias of 'iconic views' (single large objects centered in the image) by searching for pairwise combinations of object categories and scene/object pairs to collect non-iconic images with contextual relationships.
rai:dataCollection: Images were collected from Flickr by searching for pairs of object categories or scene/object category pairs to find non-iconic images. An explicit filtering stage was used to remove iconic images.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Photos uploaded by amateur photographers to Flickr, with searchable metadata and keywords.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset currently only labels 'things' and not 'stuff' (materials/objects with no clear boundaries like sky or street). It also lacks annotations for the amount an instance is occluded or the location of keypoints.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Near-duplicate images were explicitly removed, and images were grouped by photographer and date taken to minimize near-duplicates across dataset splits.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Near-duplicate images were explicitly removed, and images were grouped by photographer and date taken to minimize near-duplicates across dataset splits.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset was split into two parts: the first half released in 2014, and the cumulative release in 2015. The paper states 'MS COCO will evolve and grow over time; up to date information is available online.'
rai:dataUseCases: Advancing the state-of-the-art in object recognition, scene understanding, detecting non-iconic views of objects, contextual reasoning between objects, and precise 2D localization of objects.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Near-duplicate detection was performed using GIST descriptors [43].
